issues.failure_explanation: The formal result is an existence construction using the target function and its modulus of continuity; it does not prove that the stated grade-wise optimization procedure, empirical-loss minimization, or any training dynamics find the constructed maps. The conclusion itself acknowledges that practical training dynamics remain open.

failure_location.quote: To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first rigorous theoretical guarantee that grade-wise training yields provable vanishing approximation error in deep networks.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the advertised guarantee throughout to constructive representational existence, or supply a new optimization theorem showing that a specified grade-wise training procedure recovers sufficiently good corrections.
issues.overall_effect: Claims that the paper proves vanishing error for grade-wise training, rather than merely existence of a multigrade representation, are unsupported.
issues.title: Existential approximation theorem is overclaimed as a training guarantee
issues.why_classification: The source supports only an existence guarantee; preserving the advertised training guarantee would require new optimization theory, while the alternative repair materially withdraws the paper's central guarantee type.

issues.failure_explanation: The one-step theorem supplies a fresh network beginning at the original input. It does not assert an extension property relative to an arbitrary previously frozen prefix, nor that the previous terminal feature map retains enough information to realize the fresh construction. Renaming fresh maps with indices after $n_1$ does not establish corrections of the required form composed through the existing maps $\mathcal A_1,\ldots,\mathcal A_{n_1}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove and use an extension invariant—such as an identity channel preserved by every constructed block—and strengthen the one-step result to construct new maps after any prefix satisfying that invariant.

issues.failure_explanation: At the first step the displayed rule requires the undefined set $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{MGDL}}(0)$. More generally, minimizing over $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{MGDL}}(k)$ permits all blocks in the length-$k$ composition to vary and therefore does not enforce that previously learned blocks remain fixed; its indices also conflict with the claimed optimization of the newly introduced pair $(T_{k+1},g_{k+1})$.

failure_location.quote:
Starting from $R_0 = f$, MGDL proceeds iteratively by selecting, at each grade, an atom
together with an output map $g \in \mathcal{G}$ through the optimization problem
\[
(g_{k+1}, \bme_{k+1})
\;\in\;
\argmin_{g \in \mathcal{G},\, \bme \in \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{MGDL}}(k)}
\| R_k - g \circ \bme \|.
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the search set at grade $k+1$ by the family of extensions $T_{k+1}\circ T_k^*\circ\cdots\circ T_1^*$ of the fixed learned prefix, and define the grade-one case separately with consistent indexing.
issues.overall_effect: The dictionary-based procedure is not an executable formulation of the described grade-wise frozen-block algorithm, so conclusions attributed to that optimization rule do not follow from it.
issues.title: Dictionary optimization does not define the claimed frozen-block MGDL step
issues.why_classification: The repair is localized but materially changes the optimization set and requires a precise reformulation of the greedy procedure rather than a typographical index correction alone.

issues.failure_explanation: Taking $f\equiv0$ gives $f_1=0$. Since norms are nonnegative, the required first inequality would be $\|f_2\|_p<0$, which is impossible. The construction indeed makes both positive and negative corrections zero, and its integer $n=n_{f,\varepsilon}+n_{-f,\varepsilon}$ is not defined in the zero branches.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the one-step theorem only for nonzero inputs, define empty cube families when one sign part vanishes, and add a separate routine construction or stopping convention for zero residuals in the main theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The one-step theorem is false under its stated universal quantifier, and the proof of the main theorem cannot invoke it when the initial or an intermediate residual is identically zero.
issues.title: Strict norm decrease is impossible for the zero target
issues.why_classification: This is a degenerate case that can be isolated locally without changing the nonzero-target construction, fixed width, contraction factor, or principal approximation scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
An operator $T:C(\Omega)\to C(\Omega)$ is called a \emph{positive $\varepsilon$-contraction} if for any $g\in C(\Omega)$,
\[
    \|g^{+}-Tg\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}
    \le (1-\varepsilon)\|g^{+}\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}.
\]

issues.failure_explanation: The norm inequality bounds the absolute value of $g^+-Tg$ but does not imply $Tg\le g^+$ or the asserted nonnegativity. For example, an operator can overshoot $g^+$ by an amount within the allowed norm bound. Consequently, the argument that the two errors lie in the same interval $[0,(1-\varepsilon)\|g\|_\infty]$ does not follow from the lemma's hypothesis.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the pointwise condition $0\le Tg\le g^+$ to the lemma's hypotheses, or reformulate positive contraction to include that condition.
issues.overall_effect: The symmetrization lemma is false as stated. Its later application can only be justified because the particular constructed operator is separately intended to satisfy condition (C1).
issues.title: Positive contraction definition does not imply the pointwise bounds used in symmetrization
issues.why_classification: A short local hypothesis restores the proof and is intended for the later operator, without weakening the later contraction guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: For $d\ge2$, an average of coordinatewise trapezoids is nonzero whenever even one coordinate lies in its one-dimensional support. Thus a point can lie outside $rQ$ because one coordinate is outside the dilated interval while another coordinate has $\psi=1$, giving $\Gamma_Q>0$. The claimed cube support, bounded-overlap control of the sum, vanishing on the opposite-sign region, and pointwise domination therefore fail.
